craft_notes: Sthāyin: syllable-goddess (tongue-end moving: control-of-breath: the mouth-to-breath door — goddess OF each syllable: grammatical term as goddess-name). Sanskrit: varṇe varṇe devī...jihvāgracāriṇī...prāṇasaṃyamāt...nirmalānirākārā → L4 keeps goddess-per-syllable line 1, breath-control-free line 2. Rows: row 3 (breath→unblemished). Close: form-free (nirākāra — WITHOUT-form: the block's first absolute formlessness, kept as adjective-noun). Rejected: 'phoneme goddess' — killed: syllable kept (varṇa as LETTER-syllable: the text's unit); 'breathe right' — killed: control kept (saṃyama as restraint: the discipline word IS the practice).

lines: Goddess of each syllable, tongue-end moving:
by control of breath — unblemished and form-free.
l4.sanskrit_cite: mānasaṃ cetanā śaktir ātmā ceti catuṣṭayam | yadā priye parikṣīṇaṃ tadā tad bhairavaṃ vapuḥ

reads_against.argmap: What fourfold must be wasted? → The fourfold (manas-cetanā-śakti-ātman) wasted yields Bhairava-form.
